dossier.public_summary: The 0.917-day dip repeats at the star's 0.92-day spot period with a 2486 ppm phase-curve swing and depth that changes from ~1000 to ~5150 ppm between sectors. Light centroid is on target but duration and density mismatch plus RUWE 11.99 point to close stellar variability/binaries. This is best explained by the star's own variability, not a 3.1 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Dip period is essentially equal to stellar rotation period. Phase-curve amplitude 2486 ppm (ratio_to_depth 0.8967, chi2 623.8/9) and very large variability 6551 to 19465 ppm indicate the signal is rotational spot modulation / ellipsoidal variation at the spin period, not a transit. Spot phase curves mimic dips when folded at the rotation period.

Large out-of-dip swing and stellar-density mismatch for duration 1.979 h vs central 1.187 h indicate a non-transit origin inconsistent with a planet on this M-dwarf, supporting a stellar variability binary interpretation.
reasons.value: phase_curve amplitude_ppm 2486, ratio_to_depth 0.8967, fit_log_density_ratio -1.791, star_density_penalty 8667, duration ratio 1.666, shape v_sigma -2.972 flat but fit_b 1.056e-7, ruwe 11.99

reasons.why: Depth changes by factor ~5 within same SPOC 2-min pipeline (sector 43/44 ~4700 ppm vs sector 5 ~1000 ppm), as expected when spotted variability amplitude changes with activity, not a planet with stable depth.

reasons.why: On-target and no secondary/odd-even difference cannot overcome the rotation match and large phase curve; even star-centroid signals can be stellar variability, not planets, and xgboost planet_rank 0.1 agrees the checks look planet-unlike despite similar flat-bottomed signals.
